# ForgeSworn Link

> ForgeSworn Link connects paired devices across NATs for messages, file
> transfer and replication. It uses authenticated QUIC over owner-configured
> WebSocket relays, with optional direct paths when peers consent. Tag-mode
> relays route by pair-scoped tags. The transport uses upstream `quinn` and
> `rustls`.

Use Link for an app that manages peer enrolment and chooses its own relays.
Use `link-endpoint` for streams and `link-blossom` for hash-addressed blob
fetch with optional `shelter-kit` integration.

## ForgeSworn ecosystem

- [ForgeSworn library guide](https://forgesworn.dev/llms.txt): Find related libraries, tools and integration guides by task and runtime.
- [ForgeSworn on GitHub](https://github.com/forgesworn): Browse the organisation’s public repositories.
- [Project source](https://github.com/forgesworn/forgesworn-link): Canonical source repository, documentation and release information.

## Getting Started

- [Native Rust starter](examples/paired-echo/README.md): Run `cargo run --locked` from `examples/paired-echo` to test a paired echo over loopback WSS. Copy the directory into a new app or add `link-endpoint` at the pinned git revision shown in the guide.
- [Saved pairing in a Rust app](examples/paired-files/README.md): Copy the standalone project to enrol two devices through an approved relay, verify a file transfer, and send another file after both devices load their saved pairing.
- [Paired file quickstart](docs/paired-quickstart.md): Run a sender and receiver on separate machines with a one-use invite and your chosen relay.
- [Endpoint configuration](README.md#endpoint-configuration): Configure owner-approved relay URLs, tag-mode routing and direct-path opt-in.
- [Private relay setup](docs/relay-admission.md): Issue and revoke a client grant at a self-hosted tag relay and use the grant from the saved-pair starter.

Link's Rust crates are currently consumed from git or a local path.

## Key Concepts

- **Card**: the `FSL-CARD-1` address card a node presents to a peer, encoding its node ID, relay hints and verification context.
- **Endpoint / Session / Stream**: the narrow API surface an application uses; a `Session` moves transparently between relayed and direct without the application noticing.
- **PathStatus / PathReport**: the state machine and its JSON-serialisable report, tracking `Idle`, `Relayed`, `Probing` and `Direct` with the cause of each transition.
- **Session-keyed probes**: signed UDP probes that prove a direct address belongs to the claimed peer before traffic is trusted to it.
- **Peer identity**: QUIC verifies the pinned node key on both relayed and direct paths. The WebSocket relay uses the TLS policy of its configured destination.

## API Surface

- `link-core`: `Card`, `Hint`, `VerifyContext`, `NodeId`, `TransportKey`, `PathReport`, `PathStatus`, `FailReason`, `Tag`, `TagCase`.
- `link-endpoint`: `Endpoint`, `EndpointConfig`, `Session`, `Stream`, `PairingSession`, `RelaySpec`, `RelayStatus`, `TagBook`, `RendezvousPeer`.
- `link-blossom`: a hash-addressed blob-fetch protocol over a `Session` stream, plus an optional `shelter-kit` `BlobFetcher` adapter for mirror and repair.
- `link-relay`: the `link-relay` binary, a bounded WebSocket datagram relay plus a stateless UDP reflector.
- `link-spike`: the `link-spike` binary. Start with `pair-receive` and `pair-send` for a paired file transfer.
